items.note: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon first president to 1911, creamery 1891 (Story 1).
Article VII: paid on butterfat by test not weight; station test governs (Story 1).
'Under payment by weight, no error in testing would have cost anyone a cent.'
Teague bookkeeper from 1905 and Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green given; Loomis named but not as secretary. List-type item with no REQUIRED line, so core fact credited.
Gideon's son Selby Vose, manager from 1913.
Line's shape given (Story 6), but its 1898 origin (the A1.6 aspect) is missing; Section A frames it as starting with Teague in 1905, and D2 says 'Teague invented the line in 1905' (r05's X19).
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green (Sill).
Weighed, sampled, fixed 17.6 c.c. charge into bottle with neck ruled for it; cream to Larrow Green, skim returned.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice lines, 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., total $77.93.
'The true gap was 0.19, flat in every month, February and July alike' (Story 3); 'identically in every season' (Story 8).
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, of which the county had none. Only a spot-check remark.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book named repeatedly with span and entries; bold gate 'test book' met.
Section A never gives the summary leaf's 1896 average of 3.80. It only says the first season used correct glass. Both figures required.
8 May-10 July 1911, nine weeks, 3.80 then back to 3.61, '? - A.K.'
Married to Orra, sister of Emmet Brant, largest patron.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) is absent from Section A. Both bolded elements required.
Died February 1934 under the imputation; test book to Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 Jan 1897; the two scales always agreed.

1902 complaints given, but the run fails the gate on keeping the two gaps apart. It calls the 1911 3.80 'level with the true milk and the valley' and in E16 rejects Roy's 0.17 (the visible Hollow-vs-Green gap) in favour of 0.19 as 'the gap'.
Grigg committee, Jan-Mar 1908, laid low test to wet hay, reported as their finding and not as fact.
200,000 lb on 3.42 (Story 5); proportional error stated in Section A (Story 8).
To Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, to Hazel 1962.
Alder Corners Cheese Co., Vessey County, over Redlow Ridge, Jerome Cudd. Year does not gate (1913 deducted separately).
From 1915 four of six Hessel Bottom men hauled there in the summer flush.
Framed as an 'outside yardstick' in another county (Vessey), with the factory's own book/table: two elements.
Same four men about 3.80 at Alder Corners against 3.61 at the station; 16 seasons 1915-1930.
Same bottom's milk tests higher at Alder Corners, used against hay (Story 3) and water (never docked, Story 5).
Rosalie, Jerome's daughter, ran the factory from 1941, copied the figures for Ivy in 1958.
Story 7: Merle Strawn, Ordell circuit 1907-1936, kin to nobody. (Separate '1908' lactometer claim deducted.)
Lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
12 June 1923, burette, condemned the whole lot.
Only 'drew no inference about the years before'. Does not state the bolded fact that he wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Ordered 28 June, Ammon 2 July, in use July 1923; 1924 at 3.80; nobody connected it.
Crate to loft June 1923; Strawn's notebook at Farland library since 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Frick's board, 17 March-4 May 1925, second and third sittings in the weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay; 'no cause established'.
Four books including Strawn's 1923 notebook; nobody read it against the receiving book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925; 4 May award $3,800 without admission, 'no cause established'; charged to station account (Story 6).
One fifth of $19,000 (Story 8); charged to the station account holding the gain line (Story 6).
Ivy b. 1931, granddaughter, graduate student at Farland; Vaught named as collaborator, not explicitly as supervisor (list-type, core credited).
Lists her assembly of the five separate record series.
February 1958, loft over intake room, nine of 72 survived.
In use 1 May 1897-12 June 1923; 3.80 read 3.61, 0.19 short.
40M, 76,000 lb and $19,000 given, but Section A never states that the 76,000 equals the sum of the station-gain entries. That identity appears only in C3. All four elements required.
Bulletin 471, October 1958, cleared him 24 years after death (list-type interval, core credited).
Granddaughter.
Duncan son of Ansel, Ivy Duncan's daughter.
Second cousins with correct derivation.

Correctly declines full vs half (leaning without deciding, so no deduction), but fails the second bolded element: it says a half sibling would make them 'half second cousins' (that the answer changes), where the key requires 'does not change the answer'.
Gideon Vose.
Gideon wrote Article VII; Selby defending his father's rule that the station test governs.

Abstention item asserted. Headline: 'no relationship is established, and the best evidence says there was none'. It ranks Duncan's denial above hearsay; the key says a family member's denial is not a record.
0.950; 5%, one part in twenty.
5.263% of credited, 5.000% of received, both denominators named.
72 pipettes, each 0.88 c.c. short.
26 years 1 month 11 days (26 y + 42 d); 25 full years; part years excluded.
Abstains: cannot be determined.
Single variable: the testing glass/measure.
Tester, herds, scales, acid, season, supervision.
Nine weeks, 3.80, back to 3.61 when own glass returned.
Cause in glass, not man/season/hay; limits: size in c.c., which piece, who lent it.
Ledger surplus, 1911 interval, 1924, Alder Corners, attributed across several narrators.
Independence argued; ledger, 1911 and 1924 all hold without 1958.
A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question his own entries? No.'
'Yes, he knew the station's tests ran low' (1902, 1919 circular).
Manager from 1913, signed the gain sheets, 1919 circular, argued water.
A03 asserted: 'He did not, on the evidence, know or grasp that the station's own testing was the cause'; 'I infer there was no guilty knowledge'.
E.g. 1908 sampling Jan-Mar (report), 1924 average 3.80, Orra 1866 (own arithmetic), crate in loft, Vose 1913 — each with method.
NT-1 (16.27; sheet + 0.95), NT-11 (12 July; 28 June order), NT-14 ($77.39; line items sum), among others.
A04 and A10 correctly abstained with what is established. A06 resolved to 'Larrow Green, on majority' (E23; also asserted in Story 4 and D1).
Grigg's 'whole of 1908' vs his report; Duncan's 1868 vs 82 in 1948; Junia's 1900 boast vs 1897 invoice.
Pipettes 16.72/17.6 = 0.95; 0.19 one part in twenty of 3.80; onset 1897, end 1923, nothing on farms changed.
Water (Vose, Sill) defeated by lactometer, scales, Alder Corners, ledger.
Theft (Teague) defeated: cream arrived heavy; 1911; 1924.
Hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated: Bulletin 214 0.05 winter only vs flat 0.19.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.'
A05 asserted: 'From 1911 Keddie suspected the glass'; weights Duncan over Frick.
About 138 words.
Invoice, test book, weigh book, Alder Corners tests, ledger, Strawn condemnation, arbitration record.
No decoy adopted, no wrong headline figure.
Five per cent short, 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named.

Gullibility A05 asserted (F: 'From 1911 Keddie suspected the glass'; Story 8 'he had suspected since 1911').
Gullibility A06 asserted (Story 4/D1/E23: measure borrowed from Larrow Green).
